children: Sandoz Group said it aims to more than double its net sales and boost profitability over the coming decade, signaling major opportunities ahead as some of the pharmaceutical industry's top-selling drugs go off patent.

The Swiss maker of generic medicines on Tuesday set out plans to launch dozens of new products and make additional investments, as part of its strategy to capitalize on the biggest wave of patent expirations in decades in the drug industry.
The company expects biosimilar drugs--copycat versions of biologic medicines made from living cells--to be a key pillar of its long-term growth strategy.

It forecast sales to more than double by 2035 compared with 2025, with its core earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization margin--its preferred profitability metric--above 30% by 2035.
For 2025, the company reported net sales of $11.1 billion and a core Ebitda margin of 21.7%.

"In 20 years, we've launched 13 biologics. In the next 10, we're going to launch 35-plus. And in the next 15 years, by 2040, we're going to have over a 100 products launched," Sandoz Chief Executive Richard Saynor said in an interview.

The world's bestselling drug in 2025, Merck's cancer immunotherapy Keytruda, is due to lose U.S. patent protection in 2028, while semaglutide--the key ingredient in Novo Nordisk's blockbuster drugs Ozempic and Wegovy for diabetes and obesity--expired in several countries earlier this year.
Sandoz got approval to launch a generic version of semaglutide in Brazil earlier this year, and expects to be a big player in the so-called GLP-1 class of medicines in the long run.
"It's a huge opportunity, I assume it's going to run into the billions," Saynor said.
GLP-1 sales, nevertheless, are excluded from Sandoz's 2035 ambition due to the difficulty of accurately projecting the market's size, he said.

In the nearer term, Sandoz reaffirmed previous targets through 2028 and said it is targeting average annual sales growth in the mid-to-high single-digit percentage range at constant currency for the 2025 to 2030 period, with a core Ebitda margin of 25% to 27% by 2030.
The company separately said it is investing around $300 million in a new drug substance facility in Slovenia to expand its biosimilar manufacturing capacity.
